# PEPhub

> PEPhub is a database and web interface for biological sample metadata. Metadata is
> organized as PEPs (Portable Encapsulated Projects): a sample table plus a config file,
> addressed as `namespace/project`, optionally validated against a versioned JSON schema.

**This web interface is a client-rendered single-page app.** Fetching a page over plain
HTTP returns a JavaScript shell with no content in it. If you are not executing
JavaScript, use the REST API described below instead of scraping pages.

**The API is on a different hostname than this site.** Requests to
`https://pephub.databio.org/api/...` do not reach the API; on some deployments they
return the SPA shell with a 200 status rather than an error.

## API

- Base URL: <https://pephub-api.databio.org>
- OpenAPI spec: <https://pephub-api.databio.org/openapi.json>
- Interactive docs: <https://pephub-api.databio.org/api/v1/docs>
- Version and health: <https://pephub-api.databio.org/api/v1/_version>

All API paths below are relative to the base URL. Responses are JSON. Reads are public;
writes require a token (see Authentication).

## Reading metadata

- `GET /api/v1/namespaces` — the largest namespaces
- `GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/projects` — projects in a namespace
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{namespace}/{project}` — a single PEP
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{namespace}/{project}/annotation` — summary metadata only; prefer
  this over fetching the whole project when you just need a description or sample count
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{namespace}/{project}/samples` — the sample table
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{namespace}/{project}/config` — the project config
- `GET /api/v1/projects/{namespace}/{project}/zip` — the whole project as a zip

Projects are versioned by tag. Every project endpoint accepts `?tag=`, which defaults to
`default`. The full address form is `namespace/project:tag`.

Example:

    curl https://pephub-api.databio.org/api/v1/projects/databio/example/samples

## Search

- `POST /api/v1/search/` — search for PEPs. Backed by semantic (vector) search when
  available, falling back to SQL string matching.
- `GET /api/v1/search/namespaces` — search for namespaces

## Schemas and validation

- `GET /api/v1/schemas` — all schemas
- `GET /api/v1/schemas/{namespace}/{schema_name}` — one schema
- `GET /api/v1/schemas/{namespace}/{schema_name}/versions` — available versions
- `GET /api/v1/schemas/{namespace}/{schema_name}/versions/{semantic_version}/file` —
  download the JSON Schema itself
- `POST /api/v1/eido/validate` — validate a PEP against a schema

To produce metadata PEPhub will accept: fetch the applicable schema, fill it in, validate
against `/api/v1/eido/validate`, then submit.

## Writing metadata

- `POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/projects/json` — create a PEP from raw JSON
- `POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/projects/files` — create a PEP from files
- `PATCH /api/v1/projects/{namespace}/{project}` — update a PEP
- `POST /api/v1/projects/{namespace}/{project}/forks` — fork into your own namespace

Prefer forking into a namespace you control over writing to a curated namespace such as
`geo`.

## Bulk archives

Whole namespaces are published periodically as tar archives.

- `GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/archive` — list archives (note: singular `archive`)

The response lists each archive with a `file_path` URL on `cloud2.databio.org`, a
creation date, a project count, and a file size. That CDN host serves exact paths but
does not support directory listing, so the archive list endpoint is the only way to learn
the current filename. Archives are large; `geo` is over 1.5 GB.

## Authentication

Reads do not require authentication. For writes:

- `POST /auth/device/init` then `POST /auth/device/token` — device code flow, intended for
  headless and command-line clients
- `GET|POST|DELETE /auth/user/keys` — mint and manage long-lived API keys

Pass the token in the `Authorization` header.

## Python client

    pip install pephubclient

The `pephubclient` package wraps the endpoints above and honors a `PEPHUB_BASE_URL`
environment variable if you need to point it at another deployment.

## Related

- PEP specification: <https://pep.databio.org>
- Source code: <https://github.com/pepkit/pephub>
- Python client source: <https://github.com/pepkit/pephubclient>
